# Where RFC 5545 says a recurrence set begins and ends, stated as rules whose answers the
# specification fixes in one sentence each.
#
# name | dtstart | rrule | exdates | window start | window end | expected

# Section 3.3.10: "The UNTIL rule part defines a DATE or DATE-TIME value that bounds the
# recurrence rule in an inclusive manner. If the value specified by UNTIL is synchronized with
# the specified recurrence, this DATE or DATE-TIME becomes the last instance of the recurrence."
UNTIL on an instance is the last instance | 19970902T090000 | FREQ=DAILY;UNTIL=19970905T090000Z |  | 19970901T000000 | 19971001T000000 | 19970902T090000,19970903T090000,19970904T090000,19970905T090000
UNTIL one second before an instance excludes it | 19970902T090000 | FREQ=DAILY;UNTIL=19970905T085959Z |  | 19970901T000000 | 19971001T000000 | 19970902T090000,19970903T090000,19970904T090000

# Section 3.8.5.3: "The DTSTART property value always counts as the first occurrence" for a
# COUNT-bounded rule, and section 3.8.5.3's recurrence set never reaches before DTSTART.
COUNT=1 is DTSTART and nothing else | 19970902T090000 | FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=1 |  | 19970901T000000 | 19971001T000000 | 19970902T090000
COUNT is counted from DTSTART and not from the window | 19970902T090000 | FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=10 |  | 19970911T000000 | 19971001T000000 | 19970911T090000
the recurrence set does not reach before DTSTART | 19970902T090000 | FREQ=DAILY |  | 19970801T000000 | 19970905T000000 | 19970902T090000,19970903T090000,19970904T090000
a window entirely before DTSTART holds nothing | 19970902T090000 | FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=10 |  | 19970101T000000 | 19970201T000000 |
